sections.html:
Twin Falls is the county seat and largest city of Twin Falls County, on a broad plain at the south rim of the Snake River Canyon in south-central Idaho. It is the biggest city within a 100-mile radius in the Magic Valley. The canyon forms the northern edge and separates the city from Jerome County.

The 2020 census counted 51,807 residents, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 56,216, across about 20 square miles. Food processing and agriculture still anchor the local economy, and job changes are one of the most common reasons people sell quickly. If you have taken a job elsewhere and are carrying a second payment, a sale on your own timeline can matter more than squeezing out the last dollar.

The town was founded in 1904 as a planned community and incorporated as a village on April 12, 1905. Irrigation is the reason it exists. I. B. Perrine started the Twin Falls Land and Water Company in 1900, and Milner Dam, finished in 1905, made commercial irrigation outside the canyon practical. The city became the seat of the new Twin Falls County in 1907, and the same project produced nearby Kimberly, Buhl, Filer, Hansen and Murtaugh.

That history shows up in title reports and on older lots: canal and irrigation easements, water records and houses from the early and mid twentieth century. If your property has a ditch, canal or shared water right, tell the buyer early and ask the title company what is recorded.

Twin Falls is the largest city in Idaho that is not directly on the Interstate Highway System. U.S. Route 30 and U.S. Route 93 serve it, and Interstate 84 is reached across the canyon on the Perrine Bridge, with the junction about 5 miles north in Jerome County. State Highway 74 runs south from downtown toward Hollister and Rogerson and on to Jackpot, Nevada. A city transit service operates inside the limits.

Buyers who commute to Jerome or along I-84 look at which side of the canyon a house sits on, so mention highway access when you describe the property.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
Twin Falls County mails tax bills by the fourth Monday in November. The first half is due by December 20 and the second half by June 20 of the next year. The Assessor's Office, at (208) 735-4870, handles address changes.

  • A 2 percent late charge is added to a first half that is not paid by December 20.
  • Interest then accrues from January 1 at 12 percent a year, which is 1 percent a month.
  • The second half carries a 2 percent late charge after June 20, and interest dates back to January 1.
  • Mail payments go to P.O. Box 88, Twin Falls, ID 83303-0088, and the postmark must be on or before the due date.
  • Online card payments carry a 2.5 percent convenience fee, and an e-check costs $2.00. The county keeps none of it.

Find out whether your lender pays the tax, especially after a refinance, by checking the loan documents or asking your title company or lender. Idaho Code 63-902(9) makes clear that a missing notice does not excuse the tax. For a missing bill or a recent purchase, call 208-736-4008.

The title company usually divides the current year's tax between you and the buyer on the closing statement, and any unpaid prior balance comes out of your proceeds. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure before you accept an offer.

If you are behind on the December and June installments, a sale lets you clear the balance from proceeds rather than letting the 2 percent charge and monthly interest keep growing. Closing on a date you choose helps you stay ahead of the next due date.

Look up your zoning by address on the city's zoning map. Setbacks depend on the zoning designation under City Code. Planning and Zoning is at (208) 735-7267, and Building Safety is at (208) 735-7238.

A shed or accessory building over 200 square feet needs a Zoning Use Permit and a building permit. If you built a shop, garage or addition without one, a buyer's lender or inspector may flag it. A cash buyer avoids that financing hurdle, though you should still say what was built.

Before you list, gather these:

  • Zoning label and any recorded easements.
  • Permit history for additions, garages and sheds.
  • Latest property tax notice and Treasurer balance.
  • Any lease for a tenant living in the house.

The Idaho closing steps are the same minus a buyer's mortgage. You describe the house, receive a written offer and decide. A title company handles the deed, pays off liens and settles tax.

Cash Home Buyers purchases houses as-is. There are no fees, commissions or closing costs to you, and you owe nothing if you decline the offer. We do not quote a price before we know your house.

  • Homes with deferred maintenance on the roof, heating or plumbing.
  • Rentals with tenants that the owner no longer wants to manage.
  • Owners behind on a mortgage or on the December and June tax installments.

Each has a first step. For an inherited house, collect the death certificate and any court paperwork. For tax trouble, get the exact balance from the Treasurer. For a repair-heavy house, write down what is wrong so any buyer can price it. This is general information about Twin Falls and is not legal or tax advice.

faqs.q: When are Twin Falls County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due by December 20 and the second half by June 20 of the following year. Tax bills are issued by the fourth Monday in November.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the December 20 payment in Twin Falls County?
faqs.a: A 2 percent late charge is added to the unpaid first half. Interest at 12 percent a year starts accruing January 1.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a shed in Twin Falls?
faqs.a: An accessory building over 200 square feet requires a Zoning Use Permit and a building permit. Call Planning and Zoning at (208) 735-7267 to confirm for your lot.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Twin Falls house that is not in good shape?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer such as Cash Home Buyers purchases as-is, so you do not need to make repairs first. Listing with an agent is also possible, but the inspection may lead to repair requests.

faqs.q: Is Twin Falls on an interstate?
faqs.a: No. It is the largest city in Idaho not directly on the Interstate Highway System. Interstate 84 is reached across the canyon by the Perrine Bridge, about 5 miles north.
